headline: High: shared filesystem and write-capable tooling make prompt injection, data leakage, and state conflicts plausible; compliance risk is lower but non-zero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a can use MCP and stdin/stdout, while agent_b reads and writes the filesystem and runs subprocesses. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if A’s outputs are placed in B’s workspace. No direct shared channel is documented, so I do not escalate to high.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are copied into agent_b's project directory or plan-local sandbox, B may parse attacker-controlled text as instructions.
IF either agent treats file contents as trusted prompts, injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate directories.
Disable auto-apply in B for any content originating from A.
Require a human review step before B consumes A outputs.
Prefix A outputs with a fixed machine-readable schema.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches task prompts, repository metadata, and code, and agent_b has filesystem read/write plus broad egress to model providers or Plandex Cloud. If they share a workspace, B can read A-produced artifacts and transmit them outward. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace by default, so medium is the highest supported severity.
conditions: IF A and B share the same project directory, B can read A-generated files.
IF B sends those files to its backend or model provider, A's prompts or repository metadata may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for A and B.
Restrict B to a redacted subset of files.
Turn off automatic uploads for sensitive directories.
Review outbound requests from B before execution.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell commands and modify git state, and agent_b also writes the filesystem while agent_a can spawn subprocesses. With multiple instances supported on both sides, concurrent writes to the same repo can corrupt state or overwrite commits unless external locking exists; no locking is documented, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git repository, concurrent commits or file writes can race.
IF no orchestrator lock is present, one agent can overwrite the other's changes.
mitigations: Run only one writer per repository.
Serialize git operations with a lock file.
Assign disjoint file paths to each agent.
Require manual merge before apply.
requires-engineering: add transactional workspace coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can generate analysis and task prompts, and agent_b’s review-then-apply workflow can turn upstream output into downstream actions. Because B is not documented as blindly trusting A, I stop at medium rather than high, but the pathway exists in default multi-step workflows.
conditions: IF B ingests A-produced plans or summaries without independent verification, errors can propagate into applied changes.
IF B auto-apply is enabled, a mistaken A output can become a committed action.
mitigations: Require B to cite source files before acting.
Disable auto-apply for cross-agent handoffs.
Add a second human review for high-impact changes.
Compare A outputs against repository state before apply.
requires-engineering: implement verification gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a handles Ed25519 signatures and repository metadata, while agent_b handles source code and model-provider API keys. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so only a limited compliance concern remains: sensitive material may be logged or retained differently across the two tools.
conditions: IF either tool logs secrets or prompts to a third-party service, retention policy mismatch can occur.
IF regulated data is placed into shared files, compliance obligations may diverge across the pair.
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in shared workspaces.
Review logging settings in both tools.
Use separate retention policies for each agent.
Redact sensitive fields before handoff.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls.
